title: Boost Converter (step-up)
summary: Non-isolated step-up converter; in continuous conduction the output voltage equals the input divided by (1 - D).

ports.name: in
ports.description: Positive input supply rail feeding the inductor.

ports.name: sw
ports.description: Switching node between the inductor, the low-side switch, and the rectifier.

ports.name: out
ports.description: Regulated step-up output rail across the filter capacitor and load.

ports.name: pwm
ports.description: Gate-drive command for the low-side switch from the controller.

parameters.name: D
parameters.description: Steady-state duty cycle of the low-side switch.

parameters.name: R_load
parameters.description: Load resistance seen at the output (R_load = Vout / Iout).

parameters.name: r_L
parameters.description: Inductor series resistance (DCR); dominant loss term and the cause of the gain roll-off at high duty cycle.

parameters.name: r_C
parameters.description: Output capacitor equivalent series resistance (ESR); sets the high-frequency zero.

design_equations.name: conversion_ratio_with_losses
design_equations.expression: Vout / Vin = 1 / ((1 - D) + r_L / ((1 - D) * R_load))
design_equations.description: CCM DC conversion ratio including the inductor series resistance r_L (Alonso eq. 2.7); r_L makes the gain peak and then roll off as D -> 1 instead of rising without bound.

design_equations.name: inductor_current
design_equations.description: Average inductor current equals the input current in CCM.

design_equations.name: inductor_ripple
design_equations.description: Peak-to-peak inductor current ripple in CCM (Alonso eq. 2.35).

design_equations.name: peak_device_current
design_equations.description: Peak current through the switch, diode, and inductor in CCM.

design_equations.name: switch_peak_voltage
design_equations.description: Peak blocking voltage across the switch (and the diode) is the output voltage.

design_equations.name: output_ripple
design_equations.description: Peak-to-peak output voltage ripple in CCM (Alonso eq. 2.36); the capacitor alone supplies the load during the on-time. ESR adds r_C times the diode current step.

design_equations.name: boundary_load_resistance
design_equations.description: CCM-DCM boundary load resistance (Alonso eq. 2.38): CCM when R_load < R_lim, DCM when R_load > R_lim.

design_equations.name: boundary_output_current
design_equations.expression: Io_lim = Vout * D * (1 - D)**2 / (2 * L * fsw)
design_equations.description: Output current at the CCM-DCM boundary (Alonso eq. 2.37).

design_equations.name: dcm_conversion_ratio
design_equations.expression: Vout / Vin = (1 + sqrt(1 + 4 * D**2 / k)) / 2,  k = 2 * L * fsw / R_load
design_equations.description: DCM DC conversion ratio (Alonso eq. 2.48-2.49); load-dependent, and unlike CCM it keeps rising with D.

design_equations.name: dcm_output_ripple
design_equations.expression: dVout = L * (D * Vin / (L * fsw) - Vout / R_load)**2 / (2 * (Vout - Vin) * C)
design_equations.description: Peak-to-peak output voltage ripple in DCM (Alonso eq. 2.53).

design_equations.name: rhp_zero
design_equations.description: Right-half-plane zero frequency of Gd(s) (zero at s = (1-D)**2 * R_load / L); it adds gain while subtracting phase, so it caps the achievable loop bandwidth.

design_equations.name: ccm_characteristic_polynomial
design_equations.description: Shared CCM denominator of every small-signal transfer function below; a complex pole pair whose resonance moves with the duty cycle.

design_equations.name: control_to_output_tf_ccm
design_equations.expression: Gd(s) = Vout(s)/d(s) = Vout*R_load*(1 - D)*(1 - (L/((1 - D)**2*R_load))*s)*(1 + r_C*C*s) / Den(s)
design_equations.description: Control-to-output transfer function in CCM (Alonso eq. 2.19); note the right-half-plane zero factor (1 - (L/((1-D)**2*R_load))*s) and the ESR zero at 1/(r_C*C).

design_equations.name: audio_susceptibility_tf_ccm
design_equations.expression: Gb(s) = Vout(s)/Vin(s) = R_load*(1 - D)*(1 + r_C*C*s) / Den(s)
design_equations.description: Input-to-output (audio susceptibility) transfer function in CCM (Alonso eq. 2.22); same poles as Gd(s) but no right-half-plane zero.

design_equations.name: output_impedance_tf_ccm
design_equations.description: Open-loop output impedance in CCM (Alonso eq. 2.32); Zo(0) = 0 and Zo(inf) approx r_C.

design_equations.name: input_impedance_tf_ccm
design_equations.description: Open-loop input impedance in CCM (Alonso eq. 2.25); the characteristic polynomial appears in the numerator, with Zi(0) = (1 - D)**2*R_load and Zi(inf) -> infinity.

control_notes: The boost control-to-output transfer function Gd(s) contains a right-half-plane (RHP) zero at f_rhpz = (1-D)**2*R_load/(2*pi*L) whose frequency drops with load and duty cycle. Voltage-mode loop bandwidth must stay well below f_rhpz (typically below a third of it), which forces a slow loop. Current-mode control is preferred because it removes the inductor pole from the voltage loop, though the RHP zero remains. In discontinuous conduction (DCM, when R_load > R_lim = 2*L*fsw/(D*(1-D)**2)) the plant collapses to a first-order response and the RHP zero moves to very high frequency, so a light-load DCM design can run a faster loop. All small-signal results follow from the averaged dependent-source model: the switch is replaced by its average current source and the diode by its average voltage source, then linearized about the DC operating point.

reference.source: J. Marcos Alonso, Modelling, Control and Simulation of DC-DC Converters
